resources.string: Lets a paired tablet tap, swipe and type on this device while it is being shared. Only active while you are sharing your screen, only for a tablet you have paired, and only while you leave remote control switched on.
Mirror one tablet onto another over your local network, and drive it from there. Install this app on both tablets, give each one a role, then pair them once.
This tablet is the one being watched and controlled.
This tablet watches and drives the other one.
Opens the chooser instead of going straight back to %1$s.
Enabled. A paired tablet can tap and type here while you are sharing.
Off. Without it this tablet can still be watched, but not controlled.

While sharing, an ongoing notification stays visible on the shared tablet. Traffic never leaves your local network, and each session is encrypted with fresh keys that only the two paired tablets can derive.
Start sharing, then pair the tablet that will control this one. Only paired tablets can connect.
Sharing. Waiting for a paired tablet to connect…
No network address found. Check that Wi-Fi is on.
This tablet\'s identity: %1$s (held in secure hardware)
Screen capture was declined, so nothing is being shared.
None yet. Nothing can connect until you pair a tablet.
Ready to pair for %1$d more seconds. Connect from the other tablet now.
Let the paired tablet touch this screen
The paired tablet can tap, swipe and type here. It can do anything someone standing at this tablet could do.
Off: the paired tablet can only watch. Input from it is discarded by this tablet.
The accessibility service is on, so touches can be applied.
The accessibility service is off, so no touches can be applied.
Low — 960px, easiest on a weak network
Native resolution — sharpest, needs a fast link

Only tick this while the other tablet is showing "ready to pair". Both tablets will display a code for you to compare.

%1$s

On that tablet, open Tablet Mirror and check both of these:

1. "Let the paired tablet touch this screen" is switched on.
2. The accessibility service is turned on — the app offers a button for it.

You can still watch in the meantime.

%1$s is no longer paired with this tablet, so it refused the connection. Retrying will not fix that.\n\nTo pair again: on %1$s tap "Pair a tablet", then tap Connect below. Both tablets will show a code to compare. You do not have to unpair anything first.
